{"self_assessment": "Impact: My main contribution was keeping the table supplied. I made three full 40-domino runs to the boxes (120 dominoes) into the shared bin, at the start, at the two-minute mark and at the four-minute mark. Because I carried full loads, each trip was cheap per domino. The bin never ran dry, so the builders laying the top line, the belly and the lower lobe never had to stop and fetch. That kept the build moving through the whole ten minutes. At the last check about 126 of the 127 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I ran five close inspections of the tail and lobe areas. At 5:45 I spotted crowded dominoes at the start of the lower lobe and flagged them while the build was still in progress, so they could be checked before the push. Later inspections confirmed the chain carried through to both tail tips. Before the push I did a final walk of the line to check for bumped dominoes and found nothing down. I kept my restocking and checking separate from the builders' work so I wouldn't get in their way.

Collaboration: I kept the team informed with plain stock updates on the bin level. I offered to take the lower lobe, and when the team chose a different split of the work I adjusted straight away. I stayed clear of the neck and lobe while Priya was laying them, which helped avoid bumps in a tight area. I kept my messages short and useful, and I listened to the plan before I spoke.

Leadership: I took ownership of the logistics, which nobody else was covering, and I made sure the table was never short of material. I volunteered for the quality-check role and followed through on it, and I helped keep everyone calm and hands-off in the last two minutes so the finished picture stayed intact.

Overall I think the supply and verification work was a real enabler of the result. The design and most of the laying came from my teammates, and I believe I contributed roughly a quarter of the outcome.", "my_share_percent": 25}
